title: Connect — GitHub App + Nango + RepoProvider seam
intent: Realizes §3.1 access: the GitHub App requests exactly contents:read + metadata:read, Nango mints a short-lived installation token per operation (never cached, never logged), and every git-host-specific op lives behind the one thin RepoProvider interface. The cited spec means auth is minimal, per-operation, and swappable — a second git host is a new RepoProvider impl with zero downstream change; a byte-identical fetch proves the read path is faithful.
definition_of_done: Verified: scope set == {contents:read, metadata:read} exactly (extras rejected); Nango.mint called once per operation with distinct tokens and the sentinel token never appears in logs; no raw git-host call exists outside RepoProvider (static verifier rejects a bypass); a known file fetched through RepoProvider is byte-identical (sha256) to GitHub at the same SHA. NOT done if a token is cached across operations, a scope leaks, or a git-host call bypasses the provider.
acceptance: WHEN a GitHub App installation completes THE SYSTEM SHALL have requested exactly {contents:read, metadata:read}, minted the token per-operation via Nango without caching or logging it, and routed every git-host op through RepoProvider.
invariants: CON-005 call_external seam (every external call wrapped)
secrets never logged (token sentinel)
RepoProvider single-seam for git-host calls
risks: token accidentally cached in a module/class-level var
an ad-hoc subprocess('git') call added outside the provider
log line prints the Authorization header

title: Clone — per-tenant encrypted volume, blobless, no-exec
intent: Realizes §3.2: on connect the repo clones to a per-tenant encrypted persistent volume (/tenants/<tenant>/repos/<repo>/), one tenant never sharing a volume/process/index; repos above the blobless threshold use --filter=blob:none (never shallow, so git blame still resolves full history); pushes pull deltas thereafter (never re-clone). The cited spec means two hard rules hold: we never push to origin and the canonical copy never executes repo code — only Doc 05's disposable sandbox does.
definition_of_done: Verified: clone lands under the per-tenant path prefix and tenant-B's process cannot stat tenant-A's path; HEAD == expected SHA and file tree matches golden; large-repo clone carries --filter=blob:none and git blame still resolves (is-shallow == false); no 'git push' and no repo-script exec ever appear in the interceptor log (sentinel file absent); a push triggers a delta fetch/pull, not a clone. NOT done if any repo code executes or a cross-tenant read succeeds.
acceptance: WHEN a repo is connected THE SYSTEM SHALL clone it blobless (above threshold) into the per-tenant encrypted volume, never execute repo code, never push to origin, and delta-pull on subsequent pushes with git blame intact.
invariants: isolation triad (per-tenant volume/process/index)
never push to origin
canonical copy never executes repo code
encrypted at rest
risks: shallow clone accidentally used (breaks blame)
a repo hook/install runs during clone/index
cross-tenant path traversal via crafted repo name

title: Exclusions — gitleaks + policy globs + read-path redaction
intent: Realizes §3.3: after clone and after every delta pull, gitleaks scans changed files; its hits plus policy globs (.env*, keys, node_modules/, vendor/, generated) form the exclusion set. The cited spec means excluded paths stay on disk (the LSP may need a vendored type) but are never indexed, never in the graph, never in any tool result, never in a sandbox, never logged; detected secret values are additionally redacted at the read path across ALL read-path tools, not just batch_read.
definition_of_done: Verified: gitleaks runs on the changed set at clone AND at every pull; a planted secret file is in the exclusion set and appears in zero graph nodes, zero tool results (batch_read of it returns an error entry), and zero sandbox files; a detected secret value is redacted ([REDACTED]) in every read-path tool's output and never printed to logs. NOT done if a secret leaks into any artifact, result, sandbox, or log.
integration_point: services/code_intel/src/code_intel/exclusions.py (ExclusionManager.scan_after_clone / scan_after_pull / redact); read-path redaction in mcp_server.batch_read
acceptance: WHEN a clone or delta pull completes THE SYSTEM SHALL gitleaks-scan the changed files, add hits+policy-glob paths to the exclusion set, and guarantee those paths and any detected secret value never appear in the graph, any tool result, the sandbox, or logs.
invariants: secrets excluded from index/graph/results/sandbox/logs
read-path redaction universal across tools
post-exclusion tree is what the substrate/graph build parses
risks: a read-path tool other than batch_read forgets redaction
gitleaks skipped on pull (only runs at clone)
secret value logged during exclusion-set build

title: Structural substrate + dependency/call graph (mechanical, no LLM)
intent: Realizes §3.4 — the core value-add. tree-sitter tag extraction + aider-style PageRank over the tag-reference graph produces the file-coverage record and ranked (token-budgeted) overview; the dependency/call graph (graph_nodes/graph_edges, per-repo SQLite, code-managed schema) is built mechanically from the LSP call graph + tree-sitter imports — zero LLM, re-runnable on every change. The cited spec means: 100% file accounting (indexed+flagged == git ls-files), table nodes keyed table::<name> with kind=='table' (kills the endswith collision), the full edge-kind vocabulary (calls/imports/reads/writes/extends/implements + read_write), and a push triggers a FULL drop+re-extract rebuild (never in-place per-file invalidation, which misses cross-file dependents).
definition_of_done: Verified: every non-excluded source file is parsed and every golden declaration is a node (recall 1.0); PageRank scores non-null/non-negative and top-5 ordering matches golden; zero LLM calls in the build path (verifier rejects an injected call); indexed+flagged == ls-files with each row exactly one of indexed/flagged; table nodes are table::<name>/kind=='table'; extends/implements/read_write edges emitted so class-hierarchy blast radius and who_writes resolve from the ONE graph; grammarless/broken-span files flagged but still searchable; a push does a DROP-before-INSERT full rebuild; persisted schema has the §3.4 columns + 3 indexes + built_at_sha on real flask. NOT done if any LLM call, silent-absent file, wrong table-node id, or incremental invalidation appears.
integration_point: services/code_intel/src/code_intel/graph_builder.py (GraphBuilder.build); langs.py (tree-sitter); graph.py (PageRank/adjacency); graph_store.py (per-repo SQLite); orm.py (table nodes/tiers)
acceptance: WHEN the structural build runs on the post-exclusion tree THE SYSTEM SHALL emit the coverage record (indexed+flagged == ls-files), the PageRank-ranked overview, and the graph_nodes/graph_edges tables with the full edge-kind vocabulary and table::<name> nodes — mechanically, with zero LLM calls, stored in per-repo SQLite.
invariants: zero LLM in the core build (Dynamic-never-hardcoded: physics only)
indexed+flagged == ls-files (nothing silently absent)
graph in per-repo SQLite, not Postgres/SHA-versioned
ripgrep-only search backend (no Zoekt)
table node id == table::<name>, kind=='table'
risks: an LLM call sneaks into the build path
in-place per-file invalidation reintroduced (misses cross-file dependents)
table-node endswith collision
attribute/method call edges dropped
read+write co-access emitted as duplicate reads+writes instead of one read_write

title: The code_intel MCP server — 8 host-side tools (factory-per-query)
intent: Realizes §3.5/§2.3 — the in-meeting grounding surface. The graph is wrapped as a fresh, connection-bound SDK MCP server minted per query from a factory (never shared across concurrent workers). The 8 host-side read-only tools — get_dependents, who_writes, shares_table, list_entry_points, owner, find_references, lookup_referent, batch_read — answer over the per-repo SQLite graph + warm host-side LSP, mounted alongside native grep/read/glob. The cited spec means the graph POINTS and code ANSWERS: every tool returns file:line LEADS; who_writes/shares_table are 'resolved' only on tier-1 ORM stacks (Django/SQLAlchemy/Rails) and a labeled 'lower-bound' elsewhere — never a silent wrong-exact, never a fabricated blast-radius for a nonexistent table; get_dependents ranks by PageRank + truncated_count and never traverses reads-edges transitively; owner is CODEOWNERS-resolved or git-blame lower-bound; a per-meeting (tool,args) cache cuts round-trips; the mutable tools (bash/git/edit) exist only in the Workroom sandbox (no name overlap, no find_references in the sandbox manifest).
definition_of_done: Verified: two concurrent calls mint two distinct queryable server instances bound to the same immutable graph (never an empty shell); get_dependents returns the transitive reverse-dep set over the right edges, PageRank-ranked, capped with truncated_count, reads-edge depth-1 only; who_writes is 'resolved' on Django/SQLAlchemy/Rails with the exact writer set (real default table name resolves), 'lower-bound' elsewhere, 0 writers for a nonexistent table; shares_table reads reverse reads/writes edges into table::<name> and catches instance-param writes; owner is CODEOWNERS-resolved or names a real blame author lower-bound; batch_read reads <=10 files partial-failure-tolerant; lookup_referent is deterministic zero-LLM; every grounded claim has a valid file:line or an explicit not-found; find_references and the LSP surface are absent from the sandbox manifest and no tool name is duplicated host/sandbox. NOT done if a shared server, a silent wrong-exact, a fabricated blast-radius, or a duplicated/sandbox LSP tool appears.
integration_point: services/code_intel/src/code_intel/mcp_server.py (CodeIntelMCPServer + MCPServerFactory + the 8 @tool handlers); results.py result shapes; sandbox.py manifest
acceptance: WHEN the in-meeting agent calls a code_intel tool THE SYSTEM SHALL mint a fresh per-query server over the immutable graph and return file:line leads with correct honesty tags (resolved on tier-1 ORM, lower-bound elsewhere, never a silent wrong-exact), the mutable/LSP tools staying sandbox-exclusive.
invariants: graph points, code answers (every claim cited to live file:line)
never overstate (resolved vs lower-bound; never silent wrong-exact)
cited-or-abstain (explicit not-found, never silent omit)
per-query factory server, never shared
no in-sandbox LSP; no duplicated tool name
tool handlers return errors, never throw
risks: a server instance shared across concurrent workers after transport close
who_writes fabricates a lower-bound blast-radius for a nonexistent table (Law 2 failure)
reads-edge traversed transitively in get_dependents
find_references leaks into the sandbox manifest

title: Direct-answer wake turn — host-side answer API (no E2B)
intent: Realizes §2.1/§3.5 — the direct-answer wake turn (Proxy's ~1-2s path) calls the code_intel internal API over one ~50-100ms host-side hop, provisioning NO E2B sandbox and dispatching NO Workroom session. The cited spec means a bare ask ('where is X?', 'who owns src/flask/app.py?', 'what breaks if we change refunds?') is classified and routed to the right tool, the lead is confirmed by an actual batch_read at the pinned SHA, and the answer carries a real file:line citation + honesty tag — a locate-question resolves to X's DEFINITION (not a caller or changelog line), and with no live handle it abstains honestly rather than inventing a location.
definition_of_done: Verified: answer_direct returns a grounded answer with a file:line present in the pinned clone and touches neither e2b.provision nor workroom.dispatch; a bare 'where is url_for?' routes to find_definition and cites the module-level def (not a method or a caller/changelog line); an ownership ask keeps the full path and returns a real owner; p50 first-grounded-text <= 2.0s / p95 <= 4.0s on the warm direct-answer path. NOT done if the answer cites a graph edge instead of live code, provisions E2B, or fabricates a location instead of abstaining.
acceptance: WHEN a direct-answer wake turn asks a code question THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve it host-side over the code_intel API (no E2B, no Workroom), confirm the lead by reading the pinned clone, and return a real file:line citation with an honesty tag — or abstain honestly when no handle is bound.
invariants: direct path never provisions E2B / dispatches Workroom (§12.2 locus)
cited-or-abstain (real file:line or honest abstain)
graph points, code answers (citation from live read at pinned SHA)
latency SLO p50<=2s
risks: a locate-question routed to get_dependents fallback (returns a caller, not the definition)
citing a graph edge instead of a confirmed live line
answer path silently provisions a sandbox

title: Coverage read + Readiness gate — emits contracts.Readiness
intent: Realizes §3.7 — a repo may not join meetings until the layer verifies itself, emitting the canonical Readiness enum (connecting|cloning|indexing|ready|not_ready) + coverage_pct + gaps. The cited spec means the gate = 100% files classified + 100% parse on exact-supported files (excluding generated/vendor) + capability tiers pre-computed at index time + graph smoke check + indexed_at/pinned SHA. coverage_pct is a deterministic no-LLM read that is REPORTED, not a gate: a 100%-classified repo with honestly-labeled gaps is ready regardless of the ratio; otherwise not_ready with the specific gaps — never a silent partial join.
definition_of_done: Verified: every emitted Readiness value is one of the five canonical strings; the gate withholds 'ready' on a coverage gap, an unparsed exact-supported file (but not a flagged generated/vendor parse failure), or a failing graph smoke sample, and reaches 'ready' on the mirror happy-path; who_writes tiers are persisted per area at index time; a ready record carries a non-null indexed_at + 40-hex pinned SHA; coverage_pct/gaps are pure/deterministic/zero-LLM and a low-coverage fully-classified repo still reaches ready; pilot-scale flask reaches ready within 15 min of connect. NOT done if coverage_pct is read as a pass/fail threshold or a wrong enum value is emitted.
acceptance: WHEN the index build completes THE SYSTEM SHALL emit the canonical Readiness enum, reaching 'ready' only on 100% classification + exact-supported parse + tiers + graph smoke + stamped SHA, reporting (never gating on) coverage_pct + gaps.
acceptance_cmd: tests/code_intel -k 'M6 or readiness or coverage or LAT-002 or smoke_check or capability_tier'
invariants: never overstate (coverage_pct reported, not a gate; gaps honest)
readiness tied to the commit SHA it was built at
coverage read is deterministic zero-LLM
produces the canonical contracts.Readiness shape (§1.5)
risks: coverage_pct wired as a hard gate
capability tier computed at query time instead of persisted at index time
graph smoke check present but not actually gating (no-op)

title: Freshness — push webhook, full rebuild, reconcile, SHA-pin + GC
intent: Realizes §3.6/§2.4 — freshness that can't lie. A signature-validated, GUID+SHA-deduped push pulls the delta once and rebuilds the WHOLE per-repo graph off the pinned view (full rebuild is simpler AND correct; force-push/grammar-upgrade/large-changeset force it); a meeting-start ls-remote reconcile catches missed webhooks; each meeting pins to one commit (default tip, or PR head for a PR meeting) written to meetings.pinned_sha and answers there — a mid-meeting push emits 'repo advanced N commits' without mutating the pin. The cited spec means retained graph versions per active-meeting SHA, GC'd when unpinned; the per-meeting cache invalidates on push; a stale graph node (built_at_sha != pinned) is re-read live before its file:line becomes an answer (deference rule 2); uninstall hard-deletes clone+index+graph within 15 min.
definition_of_done: Verified: a bad-HMAC webhook is rejected and triggers no rebuild; a duplicate (GUID+SHA) rebuilds exactly once and the dedup memory is bounded; a push pulls the delta exactly once carrying changed_files and does a full drop+re-extract (incl. force-push/grammar-upgrade/large-changeset); meeting start reconciles ls-remote before confirming readiness and pins the default tip (or PR head); a mid-meeting push keeps R2==R1 with the pin unchanged + one notification; per-SHA graph versions are retained per live meeting and GC'd when unpinned; the cache invalidates on push; a stale node is re-read live (or abstains) before answering; uninstall deletes clone/graph/coverage within 900s. NOT done if a mid-meeting push shifts the pin, an incremental delta-apply runs on force-push, or a stale node is served confidently.
integration_point: services/code_intel/src/code_intel/webhook_handler.py (WebhookHandler.handle / _process_push / _handle_uninstall); pipeline.apply_push / rebuild_graph / graph retention + gc; meeting.py session pin + on_repo_advanced; graph_gc.py
acceptance: WHEN a validated push arrives THE SYSTEM SHALL dedup it, pull the delta once, full-rebuild the per-repo graph off the pinned view within ~10s, invalidate caches, and notify live meetings — while each meeting keeps answering at its retained pinned SHA and stale nodes are re-read live before citing.
acceptance_cmd: tests/code_intel -k 'M7 or GV or freshness or webhook or reconcile or pinned_sha or uninstall or stale_node'
invariants: full rebuild, never in-place per-file invalidation
pinned view never mutates mid-meeting
freshness deference (stale node re-read live before citing)
webhook signature validated + deduped + dedup memory bounded
uninstall leaves no stale ghost copy
risks: redundant double git-fetch per push disagreeing on changed_files
unbounded webhook dedup set (slow leak)
incremental apply attempted on a force-push (history rewrite)
graph version overwritten while a live meeting still pins it

title: Precise navigation — warm host-side LSP (Serena/solid-lsp) + fallback
intent: Realizes §3.5's one precision instrument — find_references via a warm HOST-SIDE language server (Serena/solid-lsp, one server per detected language), kept warm on connect/push for repos above the warm-LOC threshold, never run in the E2B sandbox. The cited spec means hardening is mandatory: every call under a hard ~3s timeout falling back to grep tagged 'lower-bound'; hung servers restart; the agent never blocks on a dead server; references into uninstalled third-party deps are labeled 'external-references-not-resolved' (a distinct label, never dropped, never conflated with the grep lower-bound); the same LSP is the source of the graph's calls/extends/implements edges at build time; a warmed large repo answers its first precise query in seconds.
definition_of_done: Verified: find_references returns the golden reference set tagged 'resolved' from a warm LSP; a slow LSP times out within ~3s+buffer and falls back to grep tagged 'lower-bound' (N results, never dropped, no stale LSP result); a hung server is restarted between calls; external-dep references are labeled 'external-references-not-resolved' distinctly; a non-Python symbol resolves via the multi-lang warm resolver; a >500k-LOC repo keeps its LSP warm after connect/push and the first meeting-start query returns warm within ~2s. NOT done if a timeout hangs, a fallback is mislabeled/silently dropped, or the LSP appears in the sandbox.
acceptance: WHEN find_references is called THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve exact references via the warm host-side LSP tagged 'resolved', or on timeout/unsupported fall back to grep tagged 'lower-bound' (restarting a hung server), labeling uninstalled-dep references 'external-references-not-resolved' and never running in the sandbox.
acceptance_cmd: tests/code_intel -k 'M8 or lsp or find_references or warm_resolver or CANON-004 or LAT-003 or external_ref'
invariants: LSP warm host-side only, never in-sandbox (§12.2)
hard timeout + grep fallback, agent never blocks on a dead server
never overstate (grep fallback tagged lower-bound; external refs distinctly labeled, never dropped)
the LSP is also the build-time source of calls/extends/implements edges
risks: a hung server not restarted (indefinite degradation)
grep fallback mislabeled 'resolved' or external refs conflated with lower-bound
cold LSP at meeting start causes a fallback-to-grep that looks like a capability loss

title: Pipeline orchestration + placement/static contracts + E2E estates
intent: Realizes §3 data-flow + §3.8 build-step ordering: run_full_pipeline drives connect→clone→scan→index→graph→server→readiness end-to-end, owns per-SHA graph retention and the one persistent webhook handler, and binds the server/factory the meeting and webhook lifecycles share. The cited spec (stack + CANONICAL §9/§12.6) means the static placement/backend contracts hold — all code under services/code_intel (never libs/code_intel), ripgrep-only search (no Zoekt/ES), graph in per-repo SQLite (no Postgres/SHA-versioned tables) — and the StaticAnalysisVerifier is a first-class Law-2 deliverable that mechanically proves these AND rejects negative builds (RepoProvider bypass, LLM-in-graph-build, fabricated 'resolved'). The two calibration estates (flask happy-path golden, messy abstention golden) prove the whole assembly on real repos.
definition_of_done: Verified: no Python module exists under libs/code_intel; no Zoekt/ElasticSearch import or subprocess appears and rg is the only search binary; all graph writes go to per-repo *.db with no psycopg2/asyncpg opened and no SHA-versioned table; the verifier exits non-zero on each negative build; the full flask pipeline reaches ready with goldens matching and zero excluded-path leaks; estate-messy abstention cases return not-found-by-this-method / lower-bound with no fabricated node or citation; SQLAlchemy and Rails tier-1 stacks resolve 'resolved'. NOT done if any placement/backend contract is violated or an estate golden fails.
acceptance: WHEN the full pipeline runs on a real estate THE SYSTEM SHALL orchestrate connect→ready end-to-end under the placement/backend static contracts (services/code_intel, ripgrep-only, per-repo SQLite), the verifier rejecting every negative build and the flask/messy estate goldens passing.
acceptance_cmd: tests/code_intel -k 'pipeline or CANON-001 or CANON-002 or CANON-003 or E2E or verifier or run_full_pipeline'

graph in per-repo SQLite (no Postgres/SHA-versioned tables)

title: Tenant isolation — graph + volume + tenant-scoped cache key (FIX)
intent: Realizes the isolation triad (§3.2/§4 security) at the query and cache layer: one tenant never shares a volume, process, or index with another, and no query or cache read ever crosses the tenant boundary. The cited spec means graph queries return only the querying tenant's SQLite nodes, a path-traversal arg for tenant-B can never surface tenant-A data, and — the FIX nuance — the per-meeting result cache MUST be tenant-scoped. Today MeetingSession.tool_call keys the cache on (tool, sorted(args)) only (meeting.py L66), with no tenant_id in the key, so two tenants issuing the same (tool, args) under the same meeting server could collide (AC-INV-007). The tenant_id already flows on CodeIntelMCPServer.tenant_id and Pipeline.tenant_id; the cache key must incorporate it.
definition_of_done: Fixed + verified: the per-meeting cache key includes the tenant_id (drawn from the bound server/pipeline), so tenant-B making the same (tool, args) call receives its own result and never tenant-A's cached value (AC-INV-007 adversarial passes); get_dependents/list_entry_points as tenant-B return only tenant-B node ids (AC-INV-006); a tenant-B tool call with a path-traversal arg surfaces zero tenant-A path/content/node (AC-INV-005). NOT done if the cache key omits tenant_id, or any cross-tenant path/node/content appears in a response.
integration_point: services/code_intel/src/code_intel/meeting.py (MeetingSession.tool_call cache key — add tenant_id); mcp_server.CodeIntelMCPServer.for_tenant / tenant_id scoping; crypto.py per-tenant volume
acceptance: WHEN two tenants issue an identical (tool, args) call under the same meeting server THE SYSTEM SHALL return each tenant only its own result by keying the per-meeting cache on tenant_id, and no graph query or path-traversal arg SHALL ever surface another tenant's data.
acceptance_cmd: tests/code_intel -k 'INV-005 or INV-006 or INV-007 or tenant_cache or tenant_isolation'
invariants: isolation triad (per-tenant volume/process/index, one tenant never sharing with another)
cache key must be tenant-scoped (no cross-tenant cache collision)
graph query returns only the querying tenant's nodes
runtime tripwire on any cross-tenant read
risks: the meeting cache key (meeting.py L66) omits tenant_id — cross-tenant cache collision (the fix)
path-traversal arg escaping the per-tenant volume prefix
a shared graph instance leaking another tenant's node ids
